titleStmt.title: The case of the seizure of the boat.

head.hi: The case of the seizure of the boat.

div.p: October 1 we sent a boat from this port to Chingnampo, loaded with general household effects of a Korean family in our employ. The boatman, Choi Myung Oo, was furnished with a small American flag and a card stating for whom the boat was being sent. When the boat reached Kangsyo, 60 li from Pyeng-Yang, it was seized by the magistrates’ (Paing Han Chung’s) officials, and when the flag and card bearing the signature of W. A. Noble was presented they stated that inasmuch as the boat was hired by an American, so much the more reason for seizing it. It required two days to get a permit from the magistrate to allow the boat to pass. The permit read: “This boat is loaded with Government goods; let it pass.” The inference, of course, is that boats hired by foreigners are open to seizure whenever the magistrates’ runners see fit to do so.
This case, like the beating of Mr. Yun and others, bears the strongest evidence of a studied purpose to harass Americans residing in Pyeng-Yang.
